newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Leftist rebels kill senator in northeast Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Leftist rebels kill senator in northeast Colombia.

text.p: Suspected leftist rebels killed a Liberal Party senator and staunch ally of President Ernesto Samper in northeast Colombia on Friday, authorities said.

A local military commander blamed the attack on National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas who are waging a campaign to disrupt local and congressional elections scheduled for late this year and early next.
Jorge Cristo, 67, was shot six times as he entered his office in Cucuta, the capital of Norte de Santander province. One of his bodyguards also died in the attack.
"Behind this crime are the terrorist hands of the ELN who have been spreading their hate across our province," Col. Victor Hugo Matamorros told reporters.

A police truck later came under a hail of gunfire and grenades as it went to check reports of a vehicle thought to have been abandoned by the assassins in a working-class neighbourhood of Cucuta, known to be fiercely loyal to the ELN.
The provincial government offered a $50,000 reward for information leading to the arrest of the killers.

Cristo was one of the leading Liberal Party politicians who persuaded Samper to run for the presidency in 1994. He later defended Samper against accusations of receiving multi-million dollar donations from the Cali drug cartel to fund his election campaign.
The dead senator was the father of Juan Fernando Cristo, Colombia's ambassador to Greece, whose name also has been linked to drug trafficking.

A statement issued by the presidential office said: "President Samper energetically condemns this cowardly, terrorist action ... the enemies of Senator Cristo are the enemies of democracy, peace, the poor and of social justice."
Local media said a communique purporting to be from a right-wing paramilitary group had been distributed in Cucuta threatening attacks on "corrupt" politicians.

But paramilitary squads have never been known to operate in the province, which is one of the traditional strongholds of the Cuban-inspired ELN, Colombia's second largest guerrilla army, which was set up by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966.

"Ours is a province where the social and political situation is very difficult. Guerrilla forces are carrying out acts like these to disrupt the elections," provincial Gov. Sergio Entrena told reporters.

The attack is the latest in a wave of political violence. The ELN claimed responsibility for kidnapping six mayors in southern Narino province earlier this week and for killing another in the town of Toledo, also in Norte de Santander.

Cristo's murder came just hours before Samper was due to hold an emergency meeting with government ministers to discuss threats against election candidates and how to stem the recent wave of ELN attacks against the country's oil industry.

Earlier this year, the ELN, the larger Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebel force and right-wing paramilitary gangs warned they would stop politicians who did not share their views from campaigning in their zones of influence.
Elections will be held on Oct. 26 to choose new provincial governors, mayors, town councilors and provincial legislators. National congressional elections are scheduled for March 6.
